sources_and_applicability.assessment: The async server accepts binary Socket.IO traffic. The maintainer marks 5.16.4 as fixed for cumulative binary-attachment memory exhaustion, newer than the scanner suggested 5.16.2. No Redis/Kombu client_manager is configured in Orb, reducing applicability of the separate compromised-queue pickle advisory.

FastAPI Form/UploadFile routes expose multipart parsing. Header and preamble parsing DoS fixes apply; parse_form-only and unsafe upload-filename configuration advisories do not establish exposure in the present Starlette integration.

Orb uses fixed HS256 with server secrets, not attacker-selected algorithms or JWKS. New application-boundary tests prove malformed time claims, deep JSON nesting and unknown critical extensions produce 401. No advisory is returned for the final pin. Generated install secrets are strong; administrator-supplied short secrets still warrant configuration validation.

Orb uses AESGCM and certificate expiry inspection; PKCS7 and X509 chain-policy APIs described in several advisories are not used. The updated wheel includes newer OpenSSL. Real encryption and restore tests pass; Apple Silicon deployment installation remains to validate.

The local UNIX temporary-directory vulnerability affects developer/CI tooling, not the running API. Coordinated pytest-asyncio 1.3.0 keeps the async suite compatible; 862 tests passed under both fixed tool pins.

Current forecast and vigil loaders call torch.load(weights_only=True). The maintainer confirms that malicious checkpoints can bypass this protection before 2.10.0. Trusted local model files reduce exposure but do not close this advisory. Other records target compiler/operators not demonstrated reachable from Orb routes. Do not upgrade the model stack without FlagEmbedding/model validation.

Many records target unused model converters, testing helpers, or other tokenizer families. Orb explicitly resolves local cached models, which reduces untrusted-download exposure but does not authenticate cached artifacts or close all model/config deserialization risks. Existing FlagEmbedding 1.3.4 compatibility pin excludes >=4.50; a tested model-stack migration is required.
